body.statement:
Let \(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}}\) be selected from the dyadic grid starting at \(h_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\) in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  For a sufficiently large fixed \(C_h\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\), every cohort and every integer \(v\ge0\) with \(2^vh_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\le1\) satisfy
\[
P\{h_s^{\mathrm{iid}}>2^vh_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd}).
\]
For every fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}})^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good,iid}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s]
\le C\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}+T^{-a/d}+N^{-a/2}\}.
\]
The terminal-grid failure probability is at most \(C\exp(-cT)\), and the iid bad-sample probability is at most \(CR_\star\) along arrays with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\).  No logarithmic block length, dense-local-site condition, or upper local-mass condition is used.
body.proof_tex:
Condition on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s=z)\).  Donor independence preserves the historical-design law, and the subclass definition makes the calendar vectors independent.  For \(\ell_{z,h}\) and \(\Phi_{z,h}\) defined in the beta-selector proof, the same density, kernel, cube-geometry, and polynomial arguments give
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\le C_0h^d,
\qquad
\mathbb E[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v]\ge c_0h^d
\]
uniformly over unit vectors \(v\).  Each summand is bounded and its variance is at most \(Ch^d\).  For a centered bounded variable \(V\), expansion of the exponential series gives
\[
\mathbb Ee^{\theta V}
\le\exp\left\{\frac{\theta^2\operatorname{Var}(V)}{2(1-C|\theta|)}\right\}
\]
for sufficiently small \(|\theta|\).  Multiplication over the independent calendar indices and exponential Markov optimization yield
\[
P\left(\left|\sum_{t=1}^T\{F(X_{st})-\mathbb EF(X_{st})\}\right|>cTh^d
\,\middle|\,E_0,z\right)\le C\exp(-cTh^d)
\tag{19}
\]
for \(F=\ell_{z,h}\) and for every fixed quadratic form of \(\Phi_{z,h}\).  A fixed sphere net turns (19) into simultaneous mass and Gram bounds.  Replication cancels from \(G_s/L_s\), so
\[
P\{\text{candidate }h\text{ fails}\mid E_0,z\}
\le C\exp(-cTh^d).
\tag{20}
\]

Put \(h_0=h_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\).  The term \(T^{-1/d}\) ensures
\[
T(2^vh_0)^d\ge c2^{vd}.
\]
If the selector has not stopped by \(2^vh_0\), that candidate failed, so (20) gives the stated tail; setting \(h=1\) gives \(Ce^{-cT}\).  Tail summation and \(\sum_v2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}<\infty\) give
\[
\mathbb E[(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}})^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good,iid}}\mid E_0,z]
\le Ch_0^a
\le C\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}+T^{-a/d}+N^{-a/2}\}.
\]
A union bound over fixed \(S\), \(e^{-cT}\le CT^{-2\lambda/d}\), and the deterministic eventual inequality \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) prove the bad-event bound by \(CR_\star\).  This proves every claim directly from independent bounded concentration.
body.justification: Direct bounded concentration over independent calendar vectors gives the no-log dyadic tail and bandwidth moments.
body.gap: It applies only to the named conditional independent-calendar subclass.
body.consumer: Both iid upper-rate corollaries use it.
